nodes.description: During acute febrile or viral triggers, systemic inflammatory cytokines and metabolic stress act on vulnerable MYRF-deficient myelin sheaths, causing splitting of myelin lamellae and accumulation of fluid within intramyelinic spaces (intramyelinic edema / myelin vacuolization) across high-density commissural and deep cerebral white matter tracts, especially the corpus callosum (splenium) and bilateral centrum semiovale. Because axons and oligodendrocyte cell bodies remain viable, the intramyelinic fluid is reabsorbed as inflammation subsides, resulting in rapid and complete radiological resolution within one to two weeks.
nodes.id: Acute Reversible Intramyelinic Edema and Myelin Vacuolization

evidence.reference_title: Case report: Mild encephalitis with a reversible splenial lesion associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection in a patient with MYRF variant.
evidence.snippet: In our patient, inflammatory responses were milder than those seen in patients with MIS-C, but caused cytotoxic edema in the entire CC and cerebral white matter. This may have been related to the vulnerability of myelin maintenance associated with the MYRF variant.

nodes.description: Mature oligodendrocytes require continuous MYRF transcriptional activity to sustain expression of major structural myelin genes (such as MBP, PLP1, MAG, and MOG) and preserve compact central nervous system myelin sheath integrity. Partial loss of MYRF transcriptional activity due to heterozygous missense variation permits normal baseline myelination and neurodevelopment but leaves mature oligodendrocytes with reduced homeostatic reserve for myelin maintenance and repair.

nodes.description: MYRF encodes an endoplasmic reticulum membrane-anchored precursor protein that undergoes intramolecular chaperone auto-processing (ICA) domain-mediated homotrimerization and autoproteolytic self-cleavage to release an active N-terminal transcription factor trimer that translocates to the nucleus. In MMERV, the recurrent heterozygous missense variant c.1208A>G (p.Gln403Arg) alters a highly conserved residue within the Ndt80-like DNA-binding domain of the cleaved N-terminal fragment, significantly diminishing its transcriptional activation of downstream myelin target genes.

evidence.reference_title: A Bacteriophage tailspike domain promotes self-cleavage of a human membrane-bound transcription factor, the myelin regulatory factor MYRF.
evidence.snippet: Indeed, the intramolecular chaperone domain of MYRF facilitates its homo-oligomerization and proteolytically processes it into two halves. The N-terminal trimer, containing the DNA-binding domain, is released from the ER membrane and moves to the nucleus, where it exerts transcriptional effects.

evidence.reference_title: MYRF is a membrane-associated transcription factor that autoproteolytically cleaves to directly activate myelin genes.
evidence.snippet: Using ChIP-Seq we show that the N-terminal cleavage product directly binds the enhancer regions of oligodendrocyte-specific and myelin genes. This binding occurs via a defined DNA-binding consensus sequence and strongly promotes the expression of target genes.

evidence.reference_title: MYRF is associated with encephalopathy with reversible myelin vacuolization.
evidence.snippet: By filtering genes expressed in the corpus callosum, we identified a heterozygous c.1208A>G predicting p.Gln403Arg in the highly conserved DNA-binding domain in the myelin regulatory factor (MYRF) gene. We subsequently screened the coding regions of MYRF by Sanger sequencing in our cohort comprised of 33 sporadic cases with MERS and 3 cases in another family with extensive myelin vacuolization, and identified the same heterozygous c.1208A>G in all affected members in the second family.
